9: /// ## What it does
10: /// Checks for `for` loops that can be replaced with `yield from` expressions.
11: ///
12: /// ## Why is this bad?
13: /// If a `for` loop only contains a `yield` statement, it can be replaced with a
14: /// `yield from` expression, which is more concise and idiomatic.
15: ///
16: /// ## Example
17: /// ```python
18: /// for x in foo:
19: ///     yield x
20: /// ```
21: ///
22: /// Use instead:
23: /// ```python
24: /// yield from foo
25: /// ```
26: ///
27: /// ## Fix safety
28: /// This rule's fix is marked as unsafe, as converting a `for` loop to a `yield
29: /// from` expression can change the behavior of the program in rare cases.
30: /// For example, if a generator is being sent values via `send`, then rewriting
31: /// to a `yield from` could lead to an attribute error if the underlying
32: /// generator does not implement the `send` method.
33: ///
34: /// In most cases, however, the fix is safe, and such a modification should have
35: /// no effect on the behavior of the program.
36: ///
37: /// ## References
38: /// - [Python documentation: The `yield` statement](https://docs.python.org/3/reference/simple_stmts.html#the-yield-statement)
39: /// - [PEP 380 – Syntax for Delegating to a Subgenerator](https://peps.python.org/pep-0380/)
40: #[derive(ViolationMetadata)]
41: pub(crate) struct YieldInForLoop;
42: 
43: impl AlwaysFixableViolation for YieldInForLoop {
44:     #[derive_message_formats]
45:     fn message(&self) -> String {
46:         "Replace `yield` over `for` loop with `yield from`".to_string()
47:     }
48: 
49:     fn fix_title(&self) -> String {
50:         "Replace with `yield from`".to_string()
51:     }
52: }
53: 
54: struct YieldFromRewriter<'a> {
55:     stmt_for: &'a ast::StmtFor,
56:     range: TextRange,
57: }
58: 
59: impl<'a> YieldFromRewriter<'a> {
60:     fn new(stmt_for: &'a ast::StmtFor) -> Self {
61:         Self {
62:             stmt_for,
63:             range: stmt_for.range(),
64:         }
65:     }
66: 
67:     /// UP028
68:     fn yield_in_for_loop(&self, checker: &mut Checker) {
69:         // Intentionally omit async contexts.
70:         if skip_async(checker) {
71:             return;
72:         }
73: 
74:         let stmt_for = self.stmt_for;
75:         let ast::StmtFor {
76:             target,
77:             iter,
78:             body,
79:             orelse,
80:             is_async: _,
81:             range: _,
82:         } = stmt_for;
83: 
84:         // If there is an else statement, don't rewrite.
85:         if !orelse.is_empty() {
86:             return;
87:         }
88: 
89:         // If there's any logic besides a yield, don't rewrite.
90:         let [body] = body.as_slice() else {
91:             return;
92:         };
93: 
94:         // If the body is not a yield, don't rewrite.
95:         let Some(value) = yielded_value(body) else {
96:             return;
97:         };
98: 
99:         // If the target is not the same as the value, don't rewrite. For example, we should rewrite
100:         // `for x in y: yield x` to `yield from y`, but not `for x in y: yield x + 1`.
101:         if !is_same_expr(target, value) {
102:             return;
103:         }
104: 
105:         // If any of the bound names are used outside of the yield itself, don't rewrite.
106:         if collect_names(value).any(|name| {
107:             let semantic = checker.semantic();
108:             binding_candidates(checker, name)
109:                 // Skip unbound bindings like `del x`
110:                 .find(|&id| !semantic.binding(id).is_unbound())
111:                 .is_some_and(|binding_id| {
112:                     let binding = semantic.binding(binding_id);
113:                     binding.references.iter().any(|reference_id| {
114:                         yield_name_reference_differs(checker, *reference_id, name)
115:                     })
116:                 })
117:         }) {
118:             return;
119:         }
120: 
121:         let mut diagnostic = Diagnostic::new(YieldInForLoop, self.range);
122:         let contents = iter_source(checker, iter, self.stmt_for);
123:         let contents = format!("yield from {contents}");
124:         diagnostic.set_fix(Fix::unsafe_edit(Edit::range_replacement(
125:             contents, self.range,
126:         )));
127:         checker.diagnostics.push(diagnostic);
128:     }
129: }
130: 
131: /// UP028
132: pub(crate) fn yield_in_for_loop(checker: &mut Checker, stmt_for: &ast::StmtFor) {
133:     YieldFromRewriter::new(stmt_for).yield_in_for_loop(checker);
134: }

136: /// Return `true` if the two expressions are equivalent, and both consistent solely
137: /// of tuples and names.
138: fn is_same_expr(left: &Expr, right: &Expr) -> bool {
139:     match (&left, &right) {
140:         (Expr::Name(left), Expr::Name(right)) => left.id == right.id,
141:         (Expr::Tuple(left), Expr::Tuple(right)) => {
142:             left.len() == right.len()
143:                 && left
144:                     .iter()
145:                     .zip(right)
146:                     .all(|(left, right)| is_same_expr(left, right))
147:         }
148:         _ => false,
149:     }
150: }
151: 
152: /// Collect all named variables in an expression consisting solely of tuples and
153: /// names.
154: fn collect_names<'a>(expr: &'a Expr) -> Box<dyn Iterator<Item = &'a ast::ExprName> + 'a> {
155:     Box::new(
156:         expr.as_name_expr().into_iter().chain(
157:             expr.as_tuple_expr()
158:                 .into_iter()
159:                 .flat_map(|tuple| tuple.iter().flat_map(collect_names)),
160:         ),
161:     )
162: }
163: 
164: fn skip_async(checker: &Checker) -> bool {
165:     checker.semantic().in_async_context()
166: }
167: 
168: fn yielded_value(body: &Stmt) -> Option<&Expr> {
169:     let Stmt::Expr(ast::StmtExpr { value, range: _ }) = body else {
170:         return None;
171:     };
172:     let Expr::Yield(ast::ExprYield {
173:         value: Some(value),
174:         range: _,
175:     }) = value.as_ref()
176:     else {
177:         return None;
178:     };
179:     Some(value)
180: }
181: 
182: fn binding_candidates<'a>(
183:     checker: &'a Checker<'_>,
184:     name: &'a ast::ExprName,
185: ) -> impl Iterator<Item = ruff_python_semantic::BindingId> + 'a {
186:     checker.semantic().current_scope().get_all(name.id.as_str())
187: }
188: 
189: fn yield_name_reference_differs(
190:     checker: &Checker,
191:     reference_id: ruff_python_semantic::ResolvedReferenceId,
192:     name: &ast::ExprName,
193: ) -> bool {
194:     checker.semantic().reference(reference_id).range() != name.range()
195: }
196: 
197: fn iter_source<'a>(checker: &'a Checker<'_>, iter: &Expr, stmt_for: &ast::StmtFor) -> &'a str {
198:     checker.locator().slice(
199:         parenthesized_range(
200:             iter.into(),
201:             stmt_for.into(),
202:             checker.comment_ranges(),
203:             checker.locator().contents(),
204:         )
205:         .unwrap_or(iter.range()),
206:     )
207: }

7: /// Returns an iterator over the ranges of the optional parentheses surrounding an expression.
8: ///
9: /// E.g. for `((f()))` with `f()` as expression, the iterator returns the ranges (1, 6) and (0, 7).
10: ///
11: /// Note that without a parent the range can be inaccurate, e.g. `f(a)` we falsely return a set of
12: /// parentheses around `a` even if the parentheses actually belong to `f`. That is why you should
13: /// generally prefer [`parenthesized_range`].
14: pub fn parentheses_iterator<'a>(
15:     expr: ExpressionRef<'a>,
16:     parent: Option<AnyNodeRef>,
17:     comment_ranges: &'a CommentRanges,
18:     source: &'a str,
19: ) -> impl Iterator<Item = TextRange> + 'a {
20:     let right_tokenizer = if let Some(parent) = parent {
21:         // If the parent is a node that brings its own parentheses, exclude the closing parenthesis
22:         // from our search range. Otherwise, we risk matching on calls, like `func(x)`, for which
23:         // the open and close parentheses are part of the `Arguments` node.
24:         //
25:         // There are a few other nodes that may have their own parentheses, but are fine to exclude:
26:         // - `Parameters`: The parameters to a function definition. Any expressions would represent
27:         //   default arguments, and so must be preceded by _at least_ the parameter name. As such,
28:         //   we won't mistake any parentheses for the opening and closing parentheses on the
29:         //   `Parameters` node itself.
30:         // - `Tuple`: The elements of a tuple. The only risk is a single-element tuple (e.g., `(x,)`),
31:         //    which must have a trailing comma anyway.
32:         let exclusive_parent_end = if parent.is_arguments() {
33:             parent.end() - ")".text_len()
34:         } else {
35:             parent.end()
36:         };
37:         SimpleTokenizer::new(source, TextRange::new(expr.end(), exclusive_parent_end))
38:     } else {
39:         SimpleTokenizer::starts_at(expr.end(), source)
40:     };
41: 
42:     let right_tokenizer = right_tokenizer
43:         .skip_trivia()
44:         .take_while(|token| token.kind == SimpleTokenKind::RParen);
45: 
46:     let left_tokenizer = BackwardsTokenizer::up_to(expr.start(), source, comment_ranges)
47:         .skip_trivia()
48:         .take_while(|token| token.kind == SimpleTokenKind::LParen);
49: 
50:     // Zip closing parenthesis with opening parenthesis. The order is intentional, as testing for
51:     // closing parentheses is cheaper, and `zip` will avoid progressing the `left_tokenizer` if
52:     // the `right_tokenizer` is exhausted.
53:     right_tokenizer
54:         .zip(left_tokenizer)
55:         .map(|(right, left)| TextRange::new(left.start(), right.end()))
56: }
57: 
58: /// Returns the [`TextRange`] of a given expression including parentheses, if the expression is
59: /// parenthesized; or `None`, if the expression is not parenthesized.
60: pub fn parenthesized_range(
61:     expr: ExpressionRef,
62:     parent: AnyNodeRef,
63:     comment_ranges: &CommentRanges,
64:     source: &str,
65: ) -> Option<TextRange> {
66:     parentheses_iterator(expr, Some(parent), comment_ranges, source).last()
67: }

the same build command again the moment it started watching for changes,

builds).

already produced, instead of re-running the command. Real file changes
detected by the watcher still re-run the build command as before.

Thanks [@​skepticfx](https://redirect.github.com/skepticfx)! - Add
Durable Object-managed Containers to top-level container configuration

Wrangler now accepts `scheduling_policy: "durable_object"` in the
top-level `containers` array and creates its namespace-backed
application after the Worker upload resolves the Durable Object
namespace ID. The namespace ID is also the application ID, so repeated
deploys idempotently ensure the same application without name-based
lookup, modification, or a Containers rollout.

Durable Object-managed entries accept `class_name`, `scheduling_policy`,
an optional `name`, and an optional named `images` map. Scheduler-only
fields are rejected. Each image provides either a local `dockerfile` or
a digest-pinned managed-registry `image`. Wrangler builds or resolves
each image, waits while Cloudflare prepares it for the Containers
runtime, and uploads the resulting references with the Worker version
for access through `ctx.container.images` and
`env.EXPERIMENTAL_CLOUDFLARE_CONTAINER_IMAGES`. Local development
support for these entries is deferred to a follow-up.

Existing scheduler-backed entries and Durable Object migrations continue
to work unchanged.

With `--containers-rollout=none`, existing Workers retain their deployed
Container metadata and image binding even when local `containers` is
omitted or empty; local scheduler edits are also ignored. The upload
stops if the deployed versions cannot be recovered. Existing Workers for
Platforms dispatch scripts reject this flag before upload because their
API does not expose enough metadata to preserve Container associations
safely. First deployments can still skip Container preparation and
rollout. Without this flag, removing managed Containers, including by
omitting `containers` entirely, clears the experimental image binding
even with `keep_vars`.

`versions deploy` validates the selected versions before changing
traffic and creates their Durable Object-managed applications only after
deployment succeeds. Both `deploy` and `versions deploy` report partial
completion if application creation fails afterward, with instructions to
retry the same command.

`EXPERIMENTAL_CLOUDFLARE_CONTAINER_IMAGES` is a temporary, reserved
Wrangler binding until native Container image metadata is available. Its
class keys identify managed applications during `versions deploy`,
including classes with empty image maps. User configuration cannot
declare a binding with this name; existing versions that already use it
are treated as Container configuration.
